question: Do public institutional and primary sources identify the CvSU Bacoor fish-tissue microplastics study mentioned in ASEANO proceedings, or do they identify separate shellfish work?

targetLead.description: The 2022 ASEANO end-project forum proceedings record that CvSU said microplastics research in fish tissues in Bacoor had been conducted and that results could be shared. No study title, taxon, exact site, collection date, method, dataset, or voucher is supplied.

disambiguatingSources.finding: The official ASEANO inception workshop report (3-6 March 2020) separately lists a CvSU “microplastic study in shells (Bacoor).” It gives no study title or results. This does not establish that it is the same output as the later fish-tissue remark.

A 2021 Sustinere research paper studies cultured green mussel Perna viridis in Bacoor Bay. Its abstract reports n=63 across inner, middle, and outer bay sites. Green mussel is a bivalve, not a finfish; the paper does not identify itself as the fish-tissue study mentioned in the ASEANO forum.

A 2023 SDSSU Multidisciplinary Research Journal paper studies mussels (Perna viridis) from Bacoor City and Manila clams (Venerupis philippinarum) from Calatagan. The Bacoor samples are described by city barangays, not resolved to a named waterbody in the reviewed text. It contains no finfish study.

A 2026 DLSU-D Research Portal article describes polymer characterization of surface-water microplastics at Barangay Pulvorista, Kawit, and Barangay San Rafael IV, Noveleta. It describes water samples, not fish tissue, and does not identify itself as the CvSU Bacoor fish-tissue study. The Manila–Bacoor Bay title alone does not place either sample in Bacoor City or identify the fish-tissue lead.

checkedQueries: site:pemsea.org Bacoor fish tissue microplastics CvSU
"Levels of Microplastics in Mussels" "Bacoor City" fish tissue
retrieval.outcome: The bounded public search still did not identify the CvSU fish-tissue study mentioned by the 2022 forum. It located distinct bivalve research and a 2026 DLSU-D surface-water microplastics article at Kawit and Noveleta; neither is evidence of fish-tissue sampling or a substitute for the unnamed Bacoor study.
retrieval.possibleRelationship: The 2020 CvSU shell-study note and published Bacoor Bay bivalve articles remain unlinked to the 2022 fish-tissue remark. The 2026 DLSU-D article samples surface water at Kawit and Noveleta and is another separate environmental study. No source reviewed here cross-identifies these studies.

evidenceLimits: No finfish taxon, exact waterbody/site, sampling dates, methods, sample size, identification support, vouchers, or reuse terms are available for the ASEANO fish-tissue lead.
The 2021 Bacoor Bay paper is about cultured green mussels; it supplies shellfish environmental research context only, not a finfish occurrence or current fish-presence assertion.
The 2023 Bacoor City paper is about mussels; its reviewed description does not establish a waterbody crosswalk or identify a finfish study.
No microplastic research result establishes current water safety, seafood safety, or fishing advice.
No item-specific reuse terms for the 2020 workshop mention or the 2021/2023 article content were verified; publication approval is not granted.

The 2026 DLSU-D Manila–Bacoor Bay portal abstract describes surface-water samples at Pulvorista, Kawit, and San Rafael IV, Noveleta; its bay-system title does not make those Bacoor City fish-tissue samples.
nextAction: Joseph may review and send the unsent inquiry draft to CvSU or PEMSEA. Until the project identity, taxon, exact collection site, dates, methods, voucher support, dataset, and reuse terms are documented, keep the Bacoor fish-tissue statement as an unresolved research lead only.
